I found myself in a dimly lit galley, a space cramped and filled with the inescapable tang of salt. The air was heavy with it, seeping into every crevice of the small room. To my south, a doorway slunk away, silently indicating a path I'd yet to explore. Directly beneath me, a hatch bored into the floor, hinted at an escape route down to the depths below.

In the center of the galley lay a kettle, though it seemed to be more of an immovable presence than an object in its own right. It contained no boiling liquid, nor any hint of recent use. Unable to open it, I decided to investigate its absence of contents instead, perhaps uncovering secrets hidden within the sodium-soaked depths. Yet, my exploration had been circumscribed by the kettle's unyielding stillness, a silent sentinel that, for now, remained resolutely untamed.

The kettle, a solitary occupant, seemed as if it yearned for some companionship amidst the stark emptiness.

The scent of paraffin clung to the air, a reminder of the manual labor that had once filled these quarters.

As a curious adventurer, I find myself wandering through the cold, salty corridors of this forgotten ship. Starting in a cramped galley, I've delved into its contents, discovering a damp rope and a half-full oil can. With a sudden shift, I descended into a shelves-empty store, and even ventured into a workshop, taking a functional oil can with me. Onward, I climbed a ladder to a glass observation room, where I found a logbook - most entries remained empty, a chilling reminder of moments long past.

With a brass key from a landing's floor, I ascended once more, proceeding north. Each experience brought novel discoveries, be it through examining objects or opening doors to new areas. Though the ship holds no warmth or comfort, it challenges me to trace the footsteps of its past inhabitants, unraveling the mysteries the labyrinth holds.

I've meticulously examined and interacted with items left behind - a logbook, a brass key, and an oil can. My actions revolved around opening and closing the brass key, turning it once, and finally using it to open a door – a ladder leading to an unknown upper storey. Afterward, I climbed back down and explored the last reachable area - the landing. Here, I checked a key that appeared to be locked but turned freely. I subsequently opened it and, with it, unlocked a staircase leading north - a path yet to be fully explored.
